Created by `brew bump` --- Created with `brew bump-formula-pr`.
release notes 
This is an ABI-compatible update for the 2.3.x series that includes all fixes since the 2.3.1 release.

In particular, this release fixes two crashes:

1. Certain older (generally 7-12 year old) CPUs including Intel x86-64 (Sandy Bridge and Ivy Bridge) and Intel Atom (Goldmont/Apollo Lake) microarchitectures that support SSE 4.2 SIMD instructions but do not support the initial AVX set and XSAVE, or other CPUs where the OS has disabled AVX and XSAVE support, will crash when trying to evaluate a Lut1D or Lut3D in OCIO libraries compiled with SSE enabled (which is the default). More recent CPUs (e.g., those supporting AVX2 or higher) should not be affected.

2. Users of the Linux Python bindings via PyPI will crash when trying to use OCIO from within another application that has been compiled with the new libstdc++ ABI, per the requirements of the VFX Platform for CY2023 and CY2024.

Bug fixes and minor enhancements:

PR #1935, Prevent trying to use AVX instructions on certain CPUs that don't support them 
PR #1933, Add manylinux_2_28 Python wheels for compliance with the current VFX Platform libstdc++ ABI
PR #1929, Fix ssse3 detection typo
PR #1921, Fix build break with custom PyString installs by always using system include pystring.h
PR #1924, Fix narrowing conversion error in unit test on riscv64
PR #1925, Enhance the ociochecklut command-line tool to print the output after each step

Many thanks to the following contributors:

@brechtvl, Ray Molenkamp, @remia, @markreidvfx, @pennelee, @chenrui333, @wahn, Shunji Yokozawa, Wayne Arnold, @phanen, @michdolan, and @doug-walker.

# Description
Properly cleaning column names for existing columns when altering table in postgresql destination mage_integrations.


# How Has This Been Tested?
1. Create data_load block that returns uppercase column name DataFrame e.g. `[{"ID": 1,},]`

By setting this variable locally we avoid the conflicting settings which currently look like

in the generated ceph build.ninja, resulting in [pipeline build failures](https://jenkins.ceph.com/job/ceph-api/67970/consoleFull#-1418442052a811ea2-3e7b-466b-84b4-d13df7e35809)

## Proposed commit message

- Refactor the buffered and unbuffered memory queue implementations into a single object
- Use a ring buffer for both cases (previously the buffered case used a linked list of independent buffers)
- Simplify the behavior of `queue.mem.flush.min_events` so it can't starve output workers when enough data is ready (previously it interacted in complicated ways with `bulk_max_size`, now it serves as a simple maximum on allowable event batch size).

author: edemaine
body:
I gave a try at running output JS/TS through esbuild to check for validity.  It seems to work, quickly — I measured a slowdown from 8.724 seconds to 8.837 seconds, so about a 1% slowdown.

However, perhaps as expected, a lot of our code snippets are invalid, mainly because they lack context. For example:
* Lack of context: Using `yield` outside a generator function, `await` outside an `async` function, `return` outside a function, `continue`/`break` outside a loop, `super` or private fields outside a class, etc.
* Intentionally bad code like `let foo!` (which TS generates helpful error messages for)
* Doubly defined variables (easy to fix)

On the other hand, I think this found some actual bugs in our output:
* Handling of anonymous classes is incorrect; `class {}` is invalid whereas `(class {})` is valid.
* `catch (e) console.error(e)` is incorrect generated output.

So I think there's something to this testing! It just needs more work.

At this point, I wanted to ask: what do you think we should do about out-of-context examples? Some options I see:
1. Add the appropriate context, like surrounding `class`, `function`, etc., to all/most examples.
2. Add `testCase.partial` or something to indicate these examples are out of context and shouldn't be tested via esbuild (but then we lose the benefit for these tests).
3. Automatically add context. E.g., if we detect `yield` but no `function*`, add an automatic wrapper. Probably we could do reasonably well with some regular expressions. Plausibly, we could even find a universal wrapper that works in all cases, e.g. an async generator method inside a class, and always add that.
